t: Founded in 1912 after the Xinhai Revolution, it ended more than two thousand years of imperial rule in China.
Under Chiang Kai-shek’s Nationalists it reunified much of China in 1928 and resisted Japan from 1937 to 1945.
After losing the civil war in 1949 it moved to Taiwan, where martial-law rule gave way to democracy in the 1990s.
dyk: The Republic of China was a founding member of the United Nations and held one of the five permanent seats on the Security Council until 1971.
ev: The Wuchang Uprising on 10 October begins the Xinhai Revolution
Sun Yat-sen becomes provisional president at Nanjing; the last Qing emperor abdicates
The Northern Expedition takes Beijing and the Nationalists reunify much of China
War with Japan begins after the Marco Polo Bridge Incident
Defeated in the civil war, the government moves to Taipei
UN Resolution 2758 transfers China’s seat to the People’s Republic
Martial law on Taiwan is lifted after 38 years
First direct presidential election, won by Lee Teng-hui

f.capital: Nanjing (1912); Beijing (1912–28); Nanjing (1928–49, wartime Chongqing); Taipei from 1949
f.successor: People’s Republic of China (on the mainland, 1949)
